description: Build the homepage narrative bottom half and close the page: redesign steps 12-18 (Connectors, live product demo, virtual computer section, social-proof framework, pricing, final CTA, footer). Restructure the Pricing page to the simpler plan set and update its existing test. Rewrite PublicFooter. Depends on FEAT-002 (homepage sections + home/ folder + tokens). All copy strings must match the spec exactly. No fabricated logos/testimonials/metrics.
steps: STEP 12 (Connectors): Add a homepage section (in web/src/screens/home/). Headline exactly: `Work where your work already lives.` Show connected services and a workflow crossing several of them (reuse the trust-strip integration set + a small cross-tool workflow visual). id=connectors. Only real/upcoming integrations.

STEP 13 (live product demo): MAJOR browser-frame product demonstration section. Example user request exactly: `Find our three biggest competitor announcements this week and tell the marketing team what we should react to.` Then show companion activity in real time using compact past-tense activity language (Searched, Read, Analyzed, Created, Updated, Messaged). Example content: Research Companion `Searching the web` / `18 sources reviewed`; Marketing Companion `Reviewing findings`; `Artifact created` `Competitive Brief · Sep 27`; `Messaged` `#marketing`. Render inside a browser-chrome frame. Avoid loud status badges - quiet, product-like. Selective CSS motion for activity appearing (respect prefers-reduced-motion). The interaction should communicate that AmazAI performs work, not just returns chat.

STEP 14 (virtual computer): Core differentiator section. Eyebrow/headline exactly: `Not limited to a chat box.` Large headline exactly: `Give your AI a computer.` Supporting copy exactly: `Your companions can use browsers, tools, files, and applications to complete multi-step work, not just tell you how to do it.` Layout: left = browser/application view, right = companion task + activity stream. Example content: `Maya's computer`, status `Working`, Task `Compare competitor pricing against our current plans.`, Activity: Opened website, Read pricing, Captured changes, Updating pricing analysis. Do NOT mention EC2, containers, worker queues, or backend infrastructure. id=virtual-computer (or computer).

STEP 15 (social proof framework): Build a SCALABLE case-study component with EMPTY/PLACEHOLDER slots. Do NOT fabricate customer logos, testimonials, usage counts, or performance claims. Design the section so real case studies drop in later, with slot shape: quote, company/customer, workflow before AmazAI, workflow with AmazAI, measured outcome. Render a tasteful empty/placeholder state (e.g. 'Case studies coming soon' or clearly-labeled sample-structure) rather than invented proof. id=customers or social-proof.

STEP 16 (pricing): Restructure web/src/screens/marketing/Pricing.jsx toward the simpler plan set the user specifies: Personal, Pro, Business, Enterprise (avoid excessive fragmentation). Each plan answers: Who is this for? / What level of usage does it include? / What important capability changes at this level? Keep `Start free` prominent. IMPORTANT: preserve the existing getStarted() behaviour and the Stripe checkout wiring for signed-in users; keep signed-out click => startLogin signup returnTo '/welcome'. The existing Pricing.test.jsx clicks buttons by name 'Get started' at indices [0],[1],[2] and asserts planKey 'personal_plus' for index [2]; you MUST update Pricing.test.jsx to match the new tiers/plan keys and button labels rather than deleting coverage - keep the three behaviours tested (signed-out => signup, signed-in => checkout for the exact tier clicked, failed checkout => inline error). If you introduce a homepage pricing summary section, it can link into /pricing; the /pricing page remains the source of truth.

STEP 17 (final CTA): Large-whitespace closing CTA on the homepage. Headline exactly: `Build your AI team.` Supporting line exactly: `Start with one companion. Give it a job. See what happens next.` CTA `Start free` (startLogin signup:true returnTo:'/welcome'). Generous whitespace; do not let the footer overpower it.

STEP 18 (footer): Rewrite PublicFooter in web/src/components/PublicShell.jsx. Restrained, organized groups: Product, Solutions, Resources, Developers, Company, Legal. Point links to existing routes where they exist (Product group -> homepage anchors / /product; Legal -> /legal, /terms, /privacy, etc.; Company -> /about, /contact; Resources -> /faq, /use-cases, /integrations) and do NOT invent new routes. Must not visually overpower the final CTA. Keep the copyright line.
Add CSS for all new sections to styles.css under the marketing token layer, consistent with FEAT-001/002. Re-run build and tests; keep green (including the updated Pricing.test.jsx).
acceptance_criteria: Homepage contains Connectors, live product demo (browser frame), virtual computer, social-proof framework, and final CTA sections with the EXACT copy strings from the spec.
The live demo uses compact past-tense activity language (Searched/Read/Analyzed/Created/Updated/Messaged) and quiet (not loud) status styling.
The virtual computer section never mentions EC2/containers/worker-queues/backend infra and uses the exact Maya's-computer example.
The social-proof section is a placeholder framework with NO fabricated logos/testimonials/usage/metrics.

Pricing.jsx presents Personal/Pro/Business/Enterprise with 'Start free' prominent, preserves Stripe checkout for signed-in users, and Pricing.test.jsx is updated and passing (three behaviours still covered).
PublicFooter shows the six restrained groups linking only to existing routes and does not overpower the final CTA.
npm run build is clean and npm test passes after the changes.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/AmazAI/web && export NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm && . /root/.nvm/nvm.sh && npm run build
grep the codebase to confirm no fabricated customer names/metrics were introduced in the social-proof section.
findings:
Delivered redesign steps 12-18. New home components in web/src/screens/home/: Connectors.jsx, LiveDemo.jsx, VirtualComputer.jsx, SocialProof.jsx, FinalCta.jsx (all match FEAT-002's style, reuse Companion + useReveal + .mkt tokens; no new deps). Wired into Landing.jsx <main> in narrative order: Artifacts -> Connectors -> LiveDemo -> VirtualComputer -> SocialProof -> FinalCta. CSS appended to web/src/styles.css as a 'part 2' block under the existing .mkt layer, with its own responsive + prefers-reduced-motion blocks.

VERBATIM COPY:
- (12) Connectors id=connectors: 'Work where your work already lives.' Same honest integration set as TrustStrip (Slack real; GitHub/Google Drive/Gmail/Google Calendar/Notion/Microsoft tagged Upcoming) + a 4-step workflow crossing Drive->GitHub->Notion->Slack (staggered reveal).
- (13) LiveDemo id=live-demo: browser-chrome frame; request verbatim 'Find our three biggest competitor announcements this week and tell the marketing team what we should react to.'; past-tense verbs Searched/Read/Analyzed/Created/Updated/Messaged; Research Companion 'Searching the web' / '18 sources reviewed'; Marketing Companion 'Reviewing findings'; 'Artifact created' 'Competitive Brief · Sep 27'; 'Messaged' '#marketing'. Status is quiet coloured text (.pf-demo-agent-status), not loud badges. Whole-agent stagger keyed off useReveal.
- (14) VirtualComputer id=browser-computer (matches the Product mega-menu #browser-computer link): eyebrow 'Not limited to a chat box.' + large headline 'Give your AI a computer.' + exact supporting copy. Left = static browser/pricing page (companion cursor), right = Maya's computer, status 'Working', Task 'Compare competitor pricing against our current plans.', Activity Opened website / Read pricing / Captured changes / Updating pricing analysis. NO EC2/containers/worker-queues/backend/infrastructure in rendered content (only in a comment noting they are avoided).
- (15) SocialProof id=customers: scalable placeholder framework, dashed 'Coming soon' card with the five slot labels (Quote / Company · customer / Workflow before AmazAI / Workflow with AmazAI / Measured outcome). NO fabricated logos/testimonials/usage/metrics.
- (17) FinalCta: 'Build your AI team.' + 'Start with one companion. Give it a job. See what happens next.' + 'Start free' (startLogin signup:true returnTo:'/welcome'). Generous whitespace; footer kept quieter.

(16) PRICING: web/src/screens/marketing/Pricing.jsx restructured to Personal ($19) / Pro ($49, featured) / Business ($99/seat) / Enterprise (Custom). Each card answers Who (tagline) / Usage / Unlocks. getStarted() + Stripe wiring PRESERVED (signed-out => startLogin signup returnTo '/welcome'; signed-in => api.billing.checkout({planKey}) then redirect; failed checkout => inline error; no client-built success/cancel URLs). Enterprise renders a 'Talk to sales' Link to /contact (no checkout). Plan CTA label kept as 'Get started' ON PURPOSE: the nav's own 'Start free' button also renders on this page via PublicShell, so reusing 'Start free' on plan buttons collided with it and broke getAllByRole index math -- 'Get started' stays distinct while 'Start free' remains prominent in the nav + hero copy and is the actual signed-out action. Pricing.test.jsx updated: three behaviours still covered, now Personal[0]/Pro[1]/Business[2], signed-in click asserts planKey 'business'. Added a 'Start free' FAQ entry; dropped the standalone For Teams block (Business tier covers teams now).

(18) FOOTER: PublicFooter in web/src/components/PublicShell.jsx rewritten to six restrained groups (Product, Solutions, Resources, Developers, Company, Legal) as a data-driven FOOTER_GROUPS map. Every link targets an EXISTING route or homepage anchor (no new routes): Product -> #companions/#rooms/#routines,/product,/pricing; Solutions -> /use-cases,/for-teams,/enterprise; Resources -> /how-it-works,/integrations,/faq; Developers -> /integrations,#browser-computer (closest existing pages, nothing fabricated); Company -> /about,/contact,/security; Legal -> /legal,/terms,/privacy,/cookie-policy,/acceptable-use,/security-disclosure. Copyright line '© {year} AmazFlow, LLC. All rights reserved.' kept. Footer CSS (app-token layer, ~L1562) adjusted: .public-foot-top is now brand + .public-foot-groups (3-col, collapsing to 2 then 1) so it stays a quiet sitemap, not a second hero.

MOTION: CSS transitions/keyframes + useReveal boolean only; no new deps (package.json unchanged). All entrances + the browser cursor keyframe are stilled under prefers-reduced-motion (new block at end of the part-2 CSS).

VERIFY: npm run build clean; npm test 29 files / 197 tests passing (baseline held). Did NOT touch authenticated app routes/components. FEAT-004 (mobile/a11y/SEO/perf deep pass) intentionally left. The #developer-tools/#unified-inbox/#search/#templates mega-menu anchors have no dedicated sections yet (graceful no-op landing on the homepage, as the brief permits).
